blinding_guess.why: The protocol spec and the code disagree on several listed elements: advertise.latch and advertise.queue_size are read by the advertise handler (defaults False/100) but absent from the advertise op in ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md; service_response.values is list<json> in the spec but the handler type-checks it as dict and the server emits a dict (or a str on failure); call_service.args is list<json> in the spec but the server emits a dict; for multiple subscriptions the spec says the highest queue_length is used while subscribe.py takes the minimum.

notes: Elements are rosbridge JSON protocol ops and fields carried over WebSocket, not ROS topics; the canonical names rosbridge_protocol/<op> do not correspond to any ROS package, and the ops are defined only in ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md prose and in the capability classes. No .msg/.srv/.action/.idl definition exists for them, so every definition_id is null and the two provided msg elements are written in declares with the definition_id value null (they are positively declared: registered handlers and emitted by the server). Field types in declares are taken from the spec text (ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md:437 and :468); the code differs: service_response.py:10 type-checks values as dict, call_service.py:135 emits the extract_values dict and call_service.py:149 emits str(exc); call_service.py:89 defaults args to [] and internal/services.py:106-116 accepts list or dict, while advertise_service.py:44 emits a dict. QoS is null for all ports because the elements travel as JSON over the WebSocket/TCP connection, where no ROS QoS applies. The ROS publisher that an advertise op creates has fixed QoS in code (internal/publishers.py:106-117): QoSProfile(depth=queue_size, durability=TRANSIENT_LOCAL), lifespan 1 s when not latched, depth forced to 1 when latched; reliability is not set (rclpy QoSProfile default). Only one latched client per topic is supported; a conflicting registration only logs a warning (publishers.py:233-248). Subscriptions merge queue_length by min (subscribe.py:186, docstring subscribe.py:105-106 'the lower of these is used'), whereas ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md:386-388 says highest. The advertise op section (ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md:277-295) documents only id/topic/type; latch and queue_size are undocumented there (the publish op also reads them, publish.py:63-64). Frames: control-message elements recorded as none; call_service/service_response and their args/values carry arbitrary service request/response payloads whose type is resolved at run time, so frame is null. Units recorded only for subscribe.queue_length (messages, stated in subscribe.py:105). exclusive is empty: the only exclusively bound resource found is the server's TCP listening socket (parameter port, default 9090, rosbridge_websocket.py:110,161), which is not a hardware or device handle. perm_grants values are the access-control allowlist parameters whose contents arrive at run time (declared default "" means no filtering). All seven package.xml files in the snapshot carry version 2.1.0; ros_distro is null so no dependency definition files were fetched.
